rules.rule: When Tapehead-specific features are disabled or idle, preserve upstream FT2 Clone playback, editing, saving, loading, input, and UI behavior. Report any concrete native-behavior regression introduced by the change.

Audio callback and replayer paths must remain real-time safe: do not add blocking I/O, logging, allocation/free, device operations, or unsafe cross-thread state access. Prefer the project's established snapshot or synchronization patterns and do not propose blocking the audio thread.

Validate track, pattern, row, instrument, sample, order, bus, MIDI, and allocator indices at every external or subsystem boundary. Pay special attention to zero-based C storage versus one-based UI and INI values, 16/32-channel assumptions, and signed/unsigned conversion.

Composition Baker changes must preserve musical events and source assets, honor documented capture exclusions, and fail without writing an XM when timing, allocation, pattern-count, or memory limits cannot be represented. Never silently truncate, overwrite, wrap, or drop performance data.

Standard XM output must remain readable by conventional XM players, and ordinary XM input must remain compatible. Tapehead-only commands or metadata may be preserved only in the documented Tapehead output path; validate lengths and ownership before reading or writing optional extensions.

For a behavioral fix or feature, require a focused regression test when the behavior can be exercised without physical MIDI or audio hardware, and keep scripts/test_all_native.py as the integrated acceptance gate.
